feature: Go exports by Go's rule, every var name an export
description: A Go name is exported when its first character is a Unicode upper-case letter, and every name a var spec declares is its own Value export at the spec's line. (Its decision on const specs is superseded by ADR-2611221643.)

specs.description: A function whose name starts with a non-ASCII capital is an export
specs.given: a Go file `p.go` containing `package p` on line 1 and `func Äpfel() {}` on line 3
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result contains an ExportDeclaration with file `p.go`, name `Äpfel`, line 3 and kind Function

specs.description: The Unicode rule covers types, methods, consts and vars
specs.given: a Go file `p.go` declaring `type Ωmega struct{}`, `func (o Ωmega) Ärger() {}`, `const Ñame = 1` and `var Øre = 2`, each on its own line
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result contains `Ωmega` with kind Type, `Ärger` with kind Method, and `Ñame` and `Øre` each with kind Value, each at the line where it is declared

specs.given: a Go file declaring `func Run() {}` and `var Count = 1`
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result contains `Run` with kind Function and `Count` with kind Value

specs.description: A name whose first character is a non-ASCII lower-case letter is not an export
specs.given: a Go file declaring `func äpfel() {}`, `type ωmega struct{}`, `const ärger = 1` and `var øre = 2`
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result contains no ExportDeclaration named `äpfel`, `ωmega`, `ärger` or `øre`

specs.description: A name starting with an underscore or with a lower-case ASCII letter followed by capitals is not an export
specs.given: a Go file declaring `func _Hidden() {}` and `var aPFEL = 1`
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result contains no ExportDeclaration named `_Hidden` or `aPFEL`

specs.description: Exported exactly when the first character is a Unicode upper-case letter
specs.given: any valid Go identifier `N` that is not the blank identifier, declared as `func N() {}` in a Go file
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: an ExportDeclaration named `N` is present if and only if the first character of `N` is an upper-case letter under Unicode (Rust `char::is_uppercase`), regardless of whether that character is ASCII

specs.description: An ungrouped var spec with two names exports both
specs.given: a Go file `p.go` with `package p` on line 1 and `var A, B = 1, 2` on line 3
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result contains an ExportDeclaration named `A` and one named `B`, both with file `p.go`, line 3 and kind Value

specs.description: A var spec inside a group with several names exports each at the spec's line
specs.given: a Go file with `package p` on line 1, `var (` on line 3, `C, D = 2, 3` on line 4 and `)` on line 5
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result contains `C` and `D`, each with line 4 and kind Value

specs.description: A typed multi-name var spec with no initialiser exports every name
specs.given: a Go file declaring `var X, Y, Z int` on one line
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result contains `X`, `Y` and `Z`, each at that line with kind Value

specs.description: A second name of a var spec can be a dead export
specs.given: a Go project where one file declares `var A, B = 1, 2` and another file in the project names `A` but no file other than the declaring one names `B`
specs.when: the project is analysed for dead exports
specs.then: `B` is reported as a dead export at the spec's line and `A` is not

specs.description: A var spec is not reduced to its first name
specs.given: a Go file declaring `var A, B = 1, 2`
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result is not only `A`: exactly one ExportDeclaration named `B` is present, and no name of the spec is recorded twice

specs.description: An unexported name in a var spec is not recorded
specs.given: a Go file declaring `var A, b, _ = 1, 2, 3`
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: the result contains `A` with kind Value and contains no ExportDeclaration named `b` or `_`

specs.description: Names of a var spec are not given another kind or another line
specs.given: a Go file with `var A, B = 1, 2` on line 3
specs.when: extract_exports is called on it with Language::Go
specs.then: neither `A` nor `B` has a kind other than Value, and neither has a line other than 3

specs.description: Every exported name of any var spec is its own Value export at the spec's line
specs.given: any Go var spec, grouped or ungrouped, at line L declaring names N1..Nk (k ≥ 1), with or without a type and initialiser
specs.when: extract_exports is called on the file with Language::Go
specs.then: for each Ni whose first character is a Unicode upper-case letter there is exactly one ExportDeclaration named Ni with line L and kind Value, and no ExportDeclaration is produced for any Ni that is not exported

amendments.by: Claude (agent, in craigjohnson's session; for review)
amendments.reason: S17 retired with ADR-2611221623 decision 3, superseded by ADR-2611221643 §1 (both accepted by craigjohnson; ADR-2611221623 re-accepted with S15-S18 removed). The S17 test asserted a const spec's second name is not an export, the opposite of ADR-2611221643. It leaves the file; no other test or assertion changes.
